About Astera Labs

Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions and software that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our platform software connects low-level device behavior, diagnostics, telemetry, validation, and fleet-scale manageability so customers can identify issues quickly and keep critical systems running.

The opportunity

Join the Platform Software Diagnostics team within Hardware Engineering and work at the boundary of software and hardware. You’ll help create practical tools for board and chip bring-up, production testing, validation, and data-driven debugging across Astera Labs’ product lines.

This internship is designed for someone who enjoys learning by doing: reading a specification, writing code, connecting to real hardware, running a test, investigating the result, and improving the tool or workflow. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and contribute to projects that turn low-level device behavior into reliable, understandable diagnostics.

What you’ll do

- Develop and improve diagnostic utilities in C for board and chip bring-up, including register access, initialization, device discovery, and device-health checks.

- Read schematics, specifications, register descriptions, and test output to understand expected hardware behavior and diagnose issues.

- Write Python utilities and test automation to make validation, data collection, and debugging more repeatable.

- Use Raspberry Pi-based lab systems and development tools to interact with boards, connectivity modules, and other hardware under test.

- Create or maintain tests for production and validation workflows, helping identify failures earlier and improve test coverage.

- Reproduce hardware/software issues, form hypotheses, run focused experiments, analyze evidence, and document findings.

- Collaborate with engineers across diagnostics, validation, production, and related hardware/software teams to communicate results and deliver practical fixes.

- Participate in code reviews, issue tracking, technical discussions, and documentation that make the team’s work easier to maintain and scale.

- Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.

Additional opportunities

Depending on project needs and your interests, you may also:

- Investigate test results and failure logs, improving parsing, reporting, and data visualization so engineers can understand issues faster.

- Contribute to regression and infrastructure projects, such as unit-test or pytest enablement, Jenkins workflows, time-series test data, or software-release automation.

What you bring

- Hands-on experience with C, Python, or another programming language through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.

- Curiosity about how software interacts with physical systems and a willingness to learn from schematics, specifications, registers, and test output.

- Comfort working in a Linux development environment and using Git-based workflows.

- A methodical approach to debugging: forming hypotheses, running focused tests, analyzing evidence, and documenting what you learn.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to collaborate across software and hardware disciplines.

- Ownership, persistence, and a practical mindset in an environment where the first attempt may not work.

Helpful experience

- Embedded software, device drivers, bare-metal development, or low-level debugging.

- I2C, SPI, PCIe, CXL, SerDes, signal-integrity concepts, or other hardware interfaces.

- Raspberry Pi, lab automation, test equipment, or semiconductor/networking hardware.

- Python test automation, pytest, log parsing, data analysis, or dashboard development.

- Jenkins or other continuous-integration and regression systems.

Internship experience and compensation

This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour.

U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.

Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

Astera Labs is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees. We value diverse perspectives and consider qualified candidates without regard to legally protected characteristics.

About Us

At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.

The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.

About the Summer Internship Program

Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater.

Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else.

We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer.

We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules:

Cohort #1

Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13

Cohort #2

Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10

All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements.

Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package.

About the Team

The Software team builds the software that enables Antares engineers to operate, test, and understand our reactor systems. The team works across embedded software, hardware interfaces, controls, telemetry, testing, and developer tools, connecting software with the physical hardware being designed and tested across Antares.

As a Software Engineering Intern, you will work on embedded software and the systems used to test, diagnose, and understand the behavior of Antares hardware. Your work will span software development, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and system telemetry, giving you hands-on exposure to the connection between software and physical systems.

Interns will be tasked with small starter projects, and then quickly tasked with a long-duration project that will culminate in a technical deliverable and presentation. You will be integrated and evaluated as if you are a first-year junior engineer, not just an “intern”. The bar for success here is high, and the expectation is that you’re able to smartly use your mentor and the resources around you to execute on your project and identify more issues and opportunities for improvement.

Roles and Responsibilities:

- Support the development, debugging, and testing of embedded software, including hardware interfaces, diagnostic capabilities, automated testing, and development tools.

- Perform hands-on testing and validation of hardware-in-the-loop environments, executing test procedures and evaluating system behavior against expected results.

- Reproduce and investigate software and hardware-in-the-loop failures, document results, and help identify the source of unexpected system behavior.

- Improve test coverage and validation processes based on findings from hands-on system testing.

- Improve system telemetry from source to destination by instrumenting software components and routing and validating telemetry data.

- Integrate system signals into HMI and Grafana so system health and behavior are consistently available for monitoring and troubleshooting.

Basic Qualifications:

- Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies

- Must have prior internship experience, or significant (>1yr) project team, laboratory, or research experience

Preferred Skills & Experience:

- GPA of 3.5 or above

- Experience developing, debugging, or testing embedded software

- Experience with hardware-in-the-loop testing or other hands-on software/hardware integration and validation

- Experience with software instrumentation, telemetry, or system monitoring

- Experience with HMI and/or Grafana

- Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred

- Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.)

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail

- Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams

- Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements

- Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively

Location

Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises.

Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

- Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

- Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

- Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

- Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

- Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Maps Team

Zipline builds and operates autonomous delivery systems that enable fast, reliable, and sustainable delivery for businesses and consumers, transforming how goods move in everyday commerce. To power this, the Maps Team is building out the long term scalable solutions that enable us to fly in new countries and regions as rapidly as possible. This team is responsible for building tools and services that produce artifacts used by our vehicles to fly their missions in the real world. This means the outputs from the Maps Team define the places our vehicles will fly in the world, their constraints, and provide strong priors for the real-time system on the vehicle to follow to accomplish its mission safely.

The Role

In this role you will contribute to, build, and own portions of Zipline’s Maps stack. That includes contributing to an extensible path planning service used for generating routes that are operationally flown every day. It also includes a suite of services for data generation, transformation and access for path planning and flight data analytics. Your work within the team could range from path planning algorithms, validation of artifacts for compliance with flight requirements, to spatial data generation and data transformation pipelines. Your work will help us achieve multi-objective routing and efficient spatial data ingestion and access, enabling Zipline to serve more customers around the world. From this internship, you can expect to learn about how theoretical path planning algorithms are adapted for a real world problem, and how data and spatial search interact to enable routing in air. Our ideal candidate works well in startup environments, is comfortable wearing many hats, and is excited to learn about many aspects of how Zipline’s spatial planning works today.

What You'll Do

- Work on services that generate routes and spatial planning artifacts

- Use tools to visualize and evaluate geospatial features that impact serviceability

- Work with teams to make spatial data accessible instantaneously anywhere in the world

- Improve planning algorithms to make routing fast, safe, and reliable

Examples of Previous Internship Projects

- Prototyping a new path planning algorithm to enhance long-range routes

- Incorporating a multidimensional risk data into the routing engine

- Creating tooling for generating composite Digital Elevation Models

- Building infrastructure to enable our zips to survey large areas

What You'll Bring

- Must have at least completed the second year of your Undergraduate studies. Masters and PhD students are also eligible

- Strong analytical and technical problem solving skills

- Deep understanding of algorithmic optimization

- Proficient coding and programming skills

- Understanding of automated testing practices

- Preferred experience supporting or developing novel algorithmic research

- Preferred experience with spatial data
